notes:
I couldn't write the commentary notes for Jeremiah 16, because I wasn't able to read any of the sources.

I tried to open seven pages at once: Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill, the Pulpit Commentary, Precept Austin, Adam Clarke and Matthew Henry. That batch hit the tool's usage limit before any page loaded. When I tried Enduring Word again on its own, I was told I had no more tool calls left for this turn. So I haven't read a single page. Your rules say to report only what the pages say, with a link for each point, so I haven't written anything. Notes written from memory would be exactly the gap-filling you asked me to avoid.

If you send the request again in a new message, I'll take the sources a few at a time so I stay under the limit:

1. **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:** Enduring Word, then the Bible Hub commentaries (Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit, Matthew Henry, Clarke), then Precept Austin.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Spurgeon sermons on verses 16–21, and Reformed and Lutheran pages on the "fishers and hunters" and the turning of the nations.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes, Bible Odyssey, and Catholic and Orthodox pages such as newadvent.org and catholic.com.

You could also paste the text of any pages you already have, and I'll write the verse-by-verse notes from those right away.
